payload.text: **`intent edit <kind> <id>` AND `intent browse <kind> <id>` REACH ONE MODEL THROUGH ONE SERVICE, AND THE KIND IS WHAT DISAMBIGUATES.** Measured 2026-08-29: `intent edit 1` refuses with **`1` names both a steel thread and an issue**, so the kind argument is not new syntax for its own sake -- it resolves an ambiguity the tool ALREADY reports. Measured 2026-08-29, BEFORE the shape change: `intent edit` was `edit <ADDRESS> [FILE]`, so `intent edit st 68` parsed `st` as the address and `68` as the file, and refused about the wrong thing. The shape change was therefore a deliberate surface decision belonging to the interface owner, and the register row was authored before either realiser was built. **IT HAS SINCE LANDED:** measured 2026-08-30 by ic, `intent edit <KIND> <ID> [FILE]` ships with `--editor`, `--path` and `--browser`; `intent browse <KIND> <ID>` ships; and the ambiguity refusal this row opens with no longer reproduces, because `intent edit 1` now refuses about a missing `<ID>` rather than about `1` naming two entities. **THE REQUIREMENT IS UNCHANGED AND UNSATISFIED; ONLY ITS EVIDENCE MOVED** -- the verbs shipping is not the criterion, which is that both reach ONE MODEL through ONE SERVICE, and `AT-17.6` is still to-write. **Second instance of the `AC-12.4` shape on this thread: a row carrying a dated measurement of a surface that has since moved.** The correction goes BESIDE the artefact rather than instead of it, so the record that the change was deliberate survives. Both verbs cover ST, WP and ISSUE.
